test_framework: Vitest with JSDOM (TypeScript), matching existing bot_behavior client/view test patterns
test_organization: Class per story, file per sub-epic: test/bot_behavior/test_display_instructions.ts
test_doubles: Mock only vscode webview boundary (createMockWebviewPanel) — test BotBehaviorClient and BotBehaviorView directly
parameterization: Individual it() tests per scenario — no parametrize needed, inline values sufficient for string-comparison assertions

assumptions: Test file is TypeScript (.ts), not Python (.py) — the architecture_reference project uses Vitest not pytest
File path is test/bot_behavior/test_display_instructions.ts — sub-epic 'Display Instructions' maps to this location following existing naming convention
Tests drive API design: BotBehavior.html must have instructions-panel element, BotBehaviorClient must have updateInstructionsPanel() method — both will fail initially until implemented
instructions-panel DOM fixture is added to BotBehavior.html as part of this feature implementation
testBehaviorConfigs uses 'shape' behavior (instructions: ['Shape the story map']) as the primary happy-path fixture
Empty instructions test uses inline fixture — no modification to shared testBehaviorConfigs needed
BotBehaviorView._postCurrentState() must include behaviorInstructions and actionInstructions — view tests verify this via posted message assertions
Tests follow Given/When/Then orchestrator pattern matching existing bot_behavior_test.ts style
Each test class extends or mirrors BotBehaviorTest helper pattern for fixture setup
Inline values are sufficient — instruction content is string arrays with no formula variation, so Scenario Outline adds no value
Individual scenarios are used because each case (happy path, empty state, hydration, navigation) has distinct setup and domain meaning
Happy path, edge cases (empty instructions), and error handling (stale/mixed content) are all covered
Background is used in both story test classes — all scenarios share the same precondition: panel open with behaviors and actions loaded
Domain terminology used throughout: BotBehavior, instructions-panel, instruction-item, instructions-empty, BotBehaviorHydrateData, navigateToBehavior, navigateToAction
Scenarios are in Given (state) / When (action) / Then (observable outcome) format — no Given describes an action
Test file path is test/panel/test_display_instructions.ts (panel channel, sub-epic = Display Instructions)
Scenarios cover both client-side (via hydrate message) and reactive (via navigation click) update paths

acceptance_criteria_count: Stop when criteria capture a full back-and-forth (user-system-user). Ensures atomic and testable slices.
acceptance_criteria_granularity: User-System Behavioral – Focus on each point of interaction (user input, system response). Ideal when precision in behavior is key.
acceptance_criteria_types: Behavioral primary, domain secondary – Emphasize user interactions with domain concepts as supporting context
increment_size: Keep increment as-is – Current scope is appropriate

assumptions: Instructions are already loaded into the domain (IBotBehavior) via loadBehaviors() and loadActions() — no new loading mechanism is needed at domain level
The panel (BotBehavior.html) needs a new dedicated instructions-panel section to display instructions
BotBehaviorClient can read this.currentBehavior?.instructions and this.currentAction?.instructions directly after navigation — client-side rendering is viable
BotBehaviorView._postCurrentState() should include behaviorInstructions and actionInstructions arrays to keep server and client in sync
Empty instructions arrays should result in a visible empty state placeholder, not an error or blank area
Action instructions displayed are the merged array (base instructions first, then behavior-specific instructions) — this is already handled by loadActions()

Both 'Display Selected Behavior Instructions' and 'Display Selected Action Instructions' stories share the same instructions-panel DOM element but differ in trigger (behavior selection vs action selection)
Initial panel load should show instructions for the current behavior and action via the hydration mechanism
When user navigates (Next/Back or tree click) the instructions-panel content is fully replaced — no partial or stale content retained
Stories are scoped to the Panel channel — domain and server changes needed to support the panel are captured as part of these panel-level stories
